rationale: Retain NorthLink Aviation as one development-stage airport-cargo infrastructure company, preserve Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III as controlling sponsor, and add the Barings-managed Alaska Future Fund co-investment disclosed in project materials. The airport remains the lessor rather than an equity owner, construction is phased and delayed, and no later sponsor transfer or signed exit was identified.

companyFieldUpdates.description: NorthLink Aviation LLC is developing a dedicated air-cargo campus on 120 acres at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport under a 55-year state lease. The planned infrastructure includes an approximately 90,000-square-foot warehouse and office complex, an 80-acre aircraft apron, hydrant fueling and ground-service facilities, with an ultimate design of 15 aircraft stands. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III acquired control on November 3, 2021, and the Barings-managed Alaska Future Fund was subsequently disclosed as an owner and co-investor; neither investor's exact percentage is publicly disclosed. The airport is the lessor, not an equity owner. FAA approval and groundbreaking occurred in 2023, but construction remained phased and delayed, with six stands planned by 2027 and no evidence of terminal operations by August 19, 2026. No later financing-driven control transfer, sale or signed pending exit was identified.
